The '''2013–14 Bundesliga '''was the 51st season of the [[Bundesliga]], Germany's premier [[Association football|football]] league. The season began on 9 August 2013 and the final matchday was on 10 May 2014. The winter break started on 23 December 2013 and ended on 24 January 2014.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.bundesliga.com/en/liga/news/2012/0000231862.php |title=2013/14 Bundesliga calendar released &#124; DFL – Bundesliga – official website |publisher=Bundesliga |date=30 November 2012 |access-date=20 February 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140704105745/http://www.bundesliga.com/en/liga/news/2012/0000231862.php |archive-date=4 July 2014 |url-status=dead |df=dmy-all }}</ref>

[[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]] were the defending champions and officially clinched the championship on 25 March 2014 after defeating [[Hertha BSC]], on the 27th matchday of the season. This broke their previous record from last season, where Bayern clinched the Bundesliga on matchday 28.<ref>{{cite web|url = https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/26713870|title=Hertha BSC 1 Bayern Munich 3|date=25 March 2014|work=BBC Sport|access-date=26 March 2014}}</ref>

==Teams==
A total of 18 teams were contesting the league, including 15 sides from the [[2012–13 Bundesliga|2012–13 season]] and two sides promoted directly from the [[2012–13 2. Bundesliga|2012–13 2. Bundesliga season]]. [[Fortuna Düsseldorf]] and [[Greuther Fürth]] were relegated from the Bundesliga after a single season and were replaced by [[Hertha Berlin]], 2. Bundesliga champions and runners-up [[Eintracht Braunschweig]]. Hertha made an immediate return to the top level, but Eintracht made their first appearance after 28 years in the second and third levels. The final participant was determined in the [[2012–13 Bundesliga#Relegation play-offs|two-legged play-off]], in which 16th placed Bundesliga side [[TSG 1899 Hoffenheim]] defeated [[1. FC Kaiserslautern]], who finished third in 2. Bundesliga.

==Relegation play-offs==
[[Hamburger SV]], who finished 16th, faced [[SpVgg Greuther Fürth]], the 3rd-placed [[2013–14 2. Bundesliga]] side for a two-legged play-off. The winner on [[Playoff format#Total points series (aggregate)|aggregate]] score after both matches  earned entry into the 2014–15 Bundesliga. [[Hamburger SV]] prevailed, avoiding their possible first relegation.
